rows.note: Use 盾牌 as the usual noun for a physical hand-held shield; it is the all-purpose choice for that meaning.

example.english: In ancient times, soldiers held a shield in one hand and a sword in the other.
example.traditional: 古代士兵一手拎住盾牌，一手攞劍。
example.jyutping: gu2 doi6 si6 bing1 jat1 sau2 ling1 zyu6 teon5 paai4 jat1 sau2 lo2 gim3

rows.note: Use 保護者 for a person who protects or defends, especially in formal or descriptive contexts.

example.english: In this relationship, they have always been a shield for the weaker party.
example.traditional: 喺呢段關係入面，佢一直都係弱勢一方嘅保護者。
example.jyutping: hai2 nei1 dyun6 gwaan1 hai6 jap6 min6 keoi5 jat1 zik6 dou1 hai6 joek6 sai3 jat1 fong1 ge3 bou2 wu6 ze2
